Step 1: Execution of fun1(str1, str2)
In C, arguments are passed by value. Function fun1 receives local copies of the pointer variables str1 and str2. Swapping s1 and s2 inside fun1 modifies only those local pointer copies and leaves str1 and str2 in main() untouched.
Therefore, the first printf statement prints: Hi Bye .

Step 2: Execution of fun2(&str1, &str2)
Function fun2 receives double pointers holding the memory addresses of str1 and str2. Dereferencing and swapping *s1 and *s2 inside fun2 alters the actual pointers in main(), so str1 now points to "Bye" and str2 points to "Hi".
Therefore, the second printf statement prints: Bye Hi.

Conclusion:
Combining both outputs gives Hi Bye Bye Hi, which matches Option (A).
